title: Maybe We Don't Need the Store: How Living Goods Began in Uganda
conflicts: Founding year: NPR 2016 says 2006; NBC 2013, GOOD 2011 and SSIR 2008 imply 2007; the AEJ trial paper dates the BRAC pilot to 2007 (and separately dates Living Goods' own Uganda operations from 2010 in a cost table). The story gives no founding year and dates only the 2007 pilot. Kenya role: SSIR says 'hired', Entrepreneur says 'volunteered'; the story says he 'took on' the job. Prices below market vary (10%, 20-40%, 30%, up to 40%); the story says only 'below the local shops'. Reach numbers conflict (CSMonitor: 200,000+ children treated in 2012 by 975 reps; Entrepreneur: 62,000 in 2013) and were not used; the story uses SSIR's 200 communities (2008) and the AEJ paper's village counts and 27% result.
notes: The quote challenges the commission model (virtue for its gifts); the connection notes the trial also found unpaid services rose and leaves the tension open. The AEJ PDF loads but the checker cannot read its text, so the trial figures are cross-checked against BRAC International's summary. Reflection deliberately not about laboratories.
